subphase: safe-c33 openssh block 4: ASN1_OCSP and RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP reconstruction
question: Can ASN1_OCSP and RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP be reconstructed to the AGENTS.md section 7 standard for the sites reachable from the openssh closure, and what is honestly true about their state afterwards?

candidate.head_note: the working tree is 247925538 (the merge of integrate/safe-c33) plus this subphase's uncommitted edits; no commit and no push were made
candidate.candidate_note: the binaries and install are the frozen V1 candidate, so the closure's obligation coordinates and reachable set are the same ones the committed openssh-closure.json measured. The source edits in this subphase are NOT in those binaries; the closure therefore measures the classification effect of the registry and boundary receipts, not the compiled effect of the source changes. mechanisms.state_reason: the seven reachable sites now have a safe ownership/borrow model and an explicit contract each, and two of them have no unsafe operation at all. SAFETY_DISCHARGED is not claimed: section 7 requires every remaining unsafe op to have a contract (done), every precondition to be established by a caller or ABI contract (done and enumerated) and no safe caller to reach UB (argued), but sections 15 and 21 also require independent review of the shared mechanism, which this single-author subphase cannot supply.
mechanisms.contract: Every callback this mechanism installs is invoked by a named in-crate caller that supplies a live object of the row's declared item type, borrowed for the call and never adopted, plus a live BIO or a correctly sized output cursor. Ownership crosses the ABI edge only at the two documented transitions (d2i_ocsp_nonce's decoded result and i2d_ocsp_nonce's encoder output), each stated on the fn. The one site that allocates transient storage either goes through the crate's CRYPTO_* seam (a_mbstr) or owns a frame-local buffer whose single release is its Rust drop (ocsp_add1_nonce).

mechanisms.state_reason: the four reachable sites have a stated contract each; two are no longer unsafe operations. SAFETY_DISCHARGED is not claimed: the lhash stores *mut c_void, so the element-type invariant of engine_pile_hash is maintained by module encapsulation rather than by the type system, and no independent BOUNDARY review exists.
mechanisms.contract: An owner allocated through the crate's CRYPTO_* seam is either raw storage (RawCtx, which never runs the destructor body) or validated (OwnedCtx); Drop is the block's single release and assume_init is the one validated transition. Callbacks this mechanism installs receive only values the installing module itself placed (lhash hash/compare over this module's EnginePile allocations) or no argument at all (the ex_data no-ops). The allocator seam, exported symbols and #[repr(C)] layouts are unchanged.

closure_rerun.delta_explained: BLOCKED 66 -> 75 and UNKNOWN 54 -> 45: the nine ASN1_OCSP/RUNTIME_ALLOC_OWNERSHIP obligations whose files had no boundary receipt (7 + 2) moved from UNKNOWN to BLOCKED now that the two site receipts exist. The two remaining sites (eng_table.rs:148, runtime/init.rs:1240) were already BLOCKED. DISCHARGED stays 0 by design: mechanism state is OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED, so adjudicate() case 5 returns BLOCKED, and the tool's generic reason text ('the V1 operation is uncontracted') does not reflect the new per-site contracts -- the boundary disposition (CONTRACTED) does.
closure_rerun.why_discharged_cannot_rise_yet: a DISCHARGED obligation requires either a mechanism-scope SAFETY_DISCHARGED receipt naming the exact site or a scoped-boundary discharge in CAMPAIGN-STATUS. Neither exists for these mechanisms, and AGENTS.md sections 15/21 forbid the author of a safety claim from being its sole adjudicator.
closure_rerun.union_note: the two closures carry the same 120 obligations with identical records, so the union counts equal the ssh counts (0 DISCHARGED / 75 BLOCKED / 45 UNKNOWN); the union graph was not re-run because no graph input changed.

non_claims: Neither mechanism is SAFETY_DISCHARGED. Both are OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED: the sites have contracts and an enumerated establishing caller, but no independent BOUNDARY review exists.
The closure was measured against the frozen V1 binaries, which do not contain this subphase's source edits. The BLOCKED/UNKNOWN shift measures classification only.
openssh remains REFUSED for SAFE_COMPATIBLE on MISSING_BOUNDARY_RECEIPT (31 files) and UNKNOWN_OBLIGATION (45 obligations).
The i2r/d2i/i2d contracts are established by in-crate callers; an external C caller of the exported X509V3_EXT_* entry points is bound by the OpenSSL ABI contract, which this receipt does not prove.
No cryptographic or compatibility court was re-run: no algorithm or wire behaviour changed.
